cards.power: THE SOUND-VIBRATION. Ty catches the airwaves and kicks the OSSICLE-ORCHESTRA into gear.
cards.lore: If Ty is perforated (Tympanik-Tear), the Bridge is broken. If he's sucked in (Retraction) Choles-the-Steatoma might be growing behind him.
cards.gradeReason: The Drummer is visceral and instantly embodiable — you ARE the eardrum.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon chaos. Subject: tympanic membrane as frantic drummer. Mood: vibrating, joyful chaos.

cards.power: THE POP. Earl opens up to let the middle ear breathe and equalize pressure.
cards.lore: If Earl goes on strike (Dysfunction), the ear fills with fluid (Serous-Swamp) and Ty the Drummer gets pulled into a vacuum.
cards.gradeReason: Pressure-Valve role is functional — needs context but plays well at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: valve-shaped character opening dramatically like a door. Mood: relief, release.

cards.power: THE LEVER-FORCE. Oscar takes Ty's vibration and concentrates it onto the Oval Window.
cards.lore: If Oscar gets stiff (Otosclerosis), the Stapes-Footplate gets stuck. The music stops before it hits the brain.
cards.gradeReason: Bone-Chain is mechanically clear but needs anatomy context to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: three tiny bones as interlocked chain wrestlers. Mood: mechanical precision.

cards.power: THE FLUID-WAVE. Cora turns mechanical waves into electrical Brain-Currents.
cards.lore: Cora is lined with Hair-Cell-Soldiers. If they are shell-shocked by loud noise, the high frequencies die first.
cards.gradeReason: Sensor role is clear but the transduction concept needs a beat of explanation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: spiral snail shell with tiny soldier hair-cells inside. Mood: electrical, humming.

cards.power: THE CANAL-CLOG. Ex makes the outer ear canal red, swollen, and agonizingly tender to the touch.
cards.lore: Moisture breaks down the wax-shield, letting the Bacterial Punks move in. Ex is surface-riot.
cards.gradeReason: Swimmer's Ear + Canal-Clog is immediately physical — you feel this card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon horror. Subject: bacterial punks rioting inside a red swollen ear canal. Mood: inflamed, oozing.

cards.power: THE PRESSURE-BURST. Mitch traps pus behind the drum. It hurts until the drum Pops and the pressure releases.
cards.lore: Usually follows a cold when Eustachian-Earl fails to drain the middle ear swamp.
cards.gradeReason: THE PRESSURE-BURST — every parent knows this feeling. Instant recognition, instant drama.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: bulging drum behind angry pus character. Mood: building pressure, imminent pop.

cards.power: THE DESTRUCTIVE PEARL. Choles is a skin-sac that grows where it doesn't belong, eating the Ossicle-Oscar bones as it expands.
cards.lore: Not a tumor, but a destructive cyst. If not evicted by surgery, Choles can break into the brain or the inner ear.
cards.gradeReason: The Bone-Eater who masquerades as a pearl — menacing, visceral, immediately memorable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark cartoon. Subject: pearlescent sac with teeth eating tiny bones. Mood: creepy, insidious expansion.

cards.power: THE BONE-STORM. Max is what happens when Mitch moves into the Air-Cells of the skull.
cards.lore: Mastoiditis is a surgical emergency if the Bone-honeycomb melts, the infection can reach the brain.
cards.gradeReason: Deep-Infector is strong but needs Mitch context — G2 escalation card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: infection character melting honeycomb skull cells. Mood: stormy, surgical emergency.

cards.power: THE ROOM-SPIN. Benny drops Ear-Crystals into the semicircular canals where they don't belong.
cards.lore: Gravity moves the crystals, telling the brain you're spinning when you're just lying down. Fix it with the Epley-Adjustmus.
cards.gradeReason: Crystal-Slipper + Room-Spin is instantly performative — you can physically act this out.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dizzy cartoon. Subject: raccoon dropping crystals into spinning canal. Mood: vertigo, tilted world.

cards.power: THE FLUID-FLOOD. Monty builds up too much fluid in the inner ear until the system Overloads.
cards.lore: The Attacks can last for hours. Monty is the master of Fluctuating Hearing Loss.
cards.gradeReason: Pressure-Spike is vivid but the triad (vertigo + tinnitus + hearing loss) needs context to fully perform.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: octopus flooding inner ear chamber. Mood: overwhelming pressure, episodic chaos.

cards.power: THE BALANCE-BLACKOUT. Vince inflames the balance-nerve, causing days of intense dizziness and nausea.
cards.lore: Usually viral. Unlike Monty, Vince doesn't mess with the hearing—he only sabotages the Level-Sensor.
cards.gradeReason: Balance-Blackout is immediately embodiable — the distinction from Monty is clinically crisp.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: frazzled nerve character with world spinning around. Mood: nauseating, off-balance.

cards.power: THE SLOW-GROWTH SQUEEZE. Artie is a tumor that slowly chokes the hearing and balance signals.
cards.lore: Rule of ENT: Unilateral hearing loss is Acoustic-Artie until proven otherwise by MRI.
cards.gradeReason: The lore rule is gold for boards; the slow-growth framing is good but less theatrical than other villains.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: slow-growing blob squeezing a nerve cable. Mood: creeping, insidious, slow-motion menace.

cards.power: THE AIRFLOW-BLOCK. Sam is a crooked wall that makes breathing through one side of the Nose-Tunnel impossible.
cards.lore: Often a legacy of a previous Wrestling Match (Trauma). Requires a Septoplasty-Surgical-Rebuild.
cards.gradeReason: Wrecked Wall is clear but anatomically static — works at the table but doesn't leap off the card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: crooked wall character blocking a nasal corridor. Mood: obstruction, asymmetric.

cards.power: THE PRESSURE-HEADACHE. Sid traps mucus in the skull-caves until they become Bio-Reactors.
cards.lore: Occurs when the Ostium-Exit is blocked by swelling. If Sid stays chronic, Poly-Pete moves in.
cards.gradeReason: Clogged Cave is evocative but pressure-headache framing is more descriptive than performative.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: clogged cave filled with bubbling mucus. Mood: trapped, pressurized, rank.

cards.power: THE RED LEAK. Eddie starts a blood-riot in the nose. Usually just a Bio-Pressure-Blip.
cards.lore: Posterior Eddie is the Heavyweight—he bleeds down the throat and needs Balloon-Packing to stop.
cards.gradeReason: THE RED LEAK — immediate, dramatic, everyone recognizes a nosebleed. Anterior vs posterior is a great twist.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: gushing nose character with Kiesselbach's plexus marked. Mood: dramatic, crimson chaos.

cards.power: THE GRAPE-CLOG. Pete is a fleshy, Grape-like growth that dandles in the nose, blocking smell and air.
cards.lore: Chronic inflammation-edema of the mucosa. Pete is the sign of an Allergy-War gone long-term.
cards.gradeReason: Grape-Clog is a great visual — Samter's Triad context elevates it for med students.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: grape-bunch character hanging from nasal mucosa. Mood: soft, fleshy, obstructive.

cards.power: THE WHITE-COAT RIOT. Sgt covers the tonsils in white Pus-Armor and makes swallowing feel like razor blades.
cards.lore: Usually Group A Strep. If the Sgt isn't defeated, he might send his Rheumatic-Ghost to attack the heart.
cards.gradeReason: White-Coat Riot + razor-blade swallowing — you feel this card in your throat immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon military. Subject: strep sergeant drilling white-coated tonsil troops. Mood: militant, white, painful.

cards.power: THE PUS-POCKET. Phil builds a massive abscess behind the tonsil, pushing the Uvula-Punching Bag to the side.
cards.lore: A surgical emergency! Phil needs a Needle-Aspiration-Crisis or the airway might close.
cards.gradeReason: Hot-Potato Voice + uvula displacement = immediately theatrical surgical emergency.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: pus pocket monster shoving uvula sideways. Mood: tense, bulging, emergency.

cards.power: THE AIRWAY-SLAM-DOOR. Emma swells up like a giant red cherry and closes the Respiratory-Airway-Rover.
cards.lore: Usually Hib-driven. Do not look in the throat with a tongue depressor—you might cause the final Door-Slam.
cards.gradeReason: Airway-Slam-Door is the most dramatic G1 in the deck — the tongue depressor warning is unforgettable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon horror. Subject: swollen red epiglottis slamming shut like a trap door. Mood: sudden, lethal drama.

cards.power: THE SUBGLOTTIC SQUEEZE. Chris narrows the pipe just below the vocal cords, making every breath sound like a whistle.
cards.lore: You need cool night air and steroids to calm his Squeeze.
cards.gradeReason: The Barker with a barking cough — every parent knows this sound. Instantly embodiable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: dog-like character squeezing a steeple-shaped trachea. Mood: barking, nocturnal, tight.

cards.power: THE VIBRATE-SPEAK. Cordy flaps together at high speed to create the Voice-Current.
cards.lore: If one Cordy is paralyzed, the voice becomes a Breathy-Whisper.
cards.gradeReason: Vocalist is good but True vs False Folds distinction makes this more anatomy than performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: two vocal cord characters vibrating together in harmony. Mood: musical, resonant.

cards.power: THE CALLOUS-RASPY. Sarah builds Screamer's Nodules—small callouses from too much Acoustic-Wrestling.
cards.lore: Chronic vocal abuse. Sarah needs Voice-Rest and therapy, not surgery.
cards.gradeReason: Screamer's Nodules + 'not surgery' — the clinical pearl is baked into the drama. G1 for med students.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: exhausted singer with bumpy vocal cords. Mood: hoarse, overworked, raspy.

cards.power: THE INVASIVE-GRIT. Max is a crusty growth that eats the vocal cords and spreads to the Neck-Nodes.
cards.lore: Squamous Cell Carcinoma. If Max takes over, the whole Voice-Box might have to be evicted.
cards.gradeReason: Hoarseness > 3 weeks pearl is excellent. Invasive-Grit is strong but slightly clinical.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark cartoon. Subject: crab-claw tumor gripping vocal cords with crumbling texture. Mood: gritty, invasive.

cards.power: THE ACID-SPILL. Ray is the Silent Reflux—he spills stomach acid onto the vocal cords at night.
cards.lore: Unlike GERD, Ray doesn't always cause heartburn. He just irritates the Throat-Lining until it swells.
cards.gradeReason: Silent Reflux framing is smart but the Globus/throat-clearing presentation needs context to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: sneaky acid character creeping up esophagus at night. Mood: silent, nocturnal, corrosive.

cards.power: THE CONGENITAL-LUMP. Betty is a leftover Gill-Slit from the womb that fills with fluid.
cards.lore: Betty is always on the Side. If she gets infected, she turns into an abscess.
cards.gradeReason: Gill-Slit origin story is cool but lateral neck location needs anatomy context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: fish-gill remnant cyst on a neck. Mood: watery, prehistoric, lateral.

cards.power: THE RISING-LUMP. Thad is a leftover track from when the thyroid moved from the tongue to the neck.
cards.lore: If the lump moves up when you stick out your tongue, it's Thad. Requires the Sistrunk-Extraction.
cards.gradeReason: Moves-with-tongue test is a perfect clinical pearl baked in. G2 because embryology needs setup.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: thyroglossal cyst midline character rising when tongue sticks out. Mood: embryonic, midline.

cards.power: THE GLAND-BLOCK. Stan traps saliva behind a Stone-Obstruction until the gland explodes in pain.
cards.lore: Stan loves the Submandibular gland because the saliva there is thick and runs uphill.
cards.gradeReason: Swelling-with-meals is an elegant clinical pearl. Runs-uphill lore is memorable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: duck character blocking saliva flow with a stone. Mood: blocked, mealtimes, painful.

cards.power: THE CHIPMUNK-CHEEK. Molly makes the face swell up so much the ears stick out.
cards.lore: Viral. Molly is the reason for the MMR-Shield.
cards.gradeReason: Chipmunk-Cheek is universal — instantly visual, instantly recognizable. MMR vaccination hook lands perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: chipmunk-cheeked character with bilateral puffy parotid swelling. Mood: viral, round, comic.

cards.power: THE CONDUCTION-TEST. They tell us if the problem is in the Bridge (Conductive) or the Sensor (Sensorineural).
cards.lore: Rinne: Bone > Air = Conductive. Weber: Lateralizes to bad ear = Conductive; to good ear = Sensorineural.
cards.gradeReason: The Tuning Forks as a duo-character is clever. Lore encodes the lateralization logic efficiently.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: two tuning fork characters as detective duo. Mood: investigative, vibrating, precise.

cards.power: THE CANAL-VISION. Oz allows us to look past the wax-guards and see Tympanic-Ty directly.
cards.lore: Oz is the gatekeeper. Without Oz, Mitch and Choles stay hidden in the dark.
cards.gradeReason: The Eye as a tool-character is effective. Gatekeeper framing gives it personality.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: otoscope as owl eye character peering into dark canal. Mood: illuminating, precise.

cards.power: THE THROAT-SPY. Ned snakes through the nose to look at Emma-Epiglottis and Cordy-the-Vocalist in real-time.
cards.lore: The gold standard for seeing the Airway-Runway without the patient gagging.
cards.gradeReason: Throat-Spy is a fun role but tool-cards are inherently more G2 than character-villain cards.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: flexible fiber-optic snake as a spy sneaking through nasal passage. Mood: stealthy, illuminated.

cards.power: THE HEARING-MAP. Annie draws the landscape of what the patient can hear and what is lost to the Silence-Shadows.
cards.lore: If the lines are far apart, there's an Air-Bone-Gap—proof of a conductive bridge failure.
cards.gradeReason: Hearing-Map + Silence-Shadows is poetic and immediately visual — G1 for its storytelling elegance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: cartographer character drawing hearing threshold map. Mood: mapmaking, audiological.

cards.power: THE DOUBLE-STRIKE. Cid kills the bacteria and cools down the swelling in Otitis-Externa-Ex.
cards.lore: Use it for 7 days and only use if the Drum (Ty) is intact, unless it's the Otic-Safe version!
cards.gradeReason: Cipro + Dexa double-strike is a clean mnemonic. Tympanic membrane warning is essential safety lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: dual-action ear-drop character with antibiotic sword and steroid shield. Mood: targeted, clinical.

cards.power: THE ALLERGY-BRAKE. Flo calms the Mucosal-Riot in the nose, shrinking Poly-Pete and opening Sinus-Sid.
cards.lore: Works locally. Flo doesn't start the fight, she ends it by stopping the recruitment of inflammatory cells.
cards.gradeReason: Allergy-Brake is immediately performative — she ends the fight, not starts it. Elegant and embodiable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: butterfly-shaped steroid character braking a nasal riot. Mood: calming, local, gentle.

cards.power: THE INSTANT-OPEN. Oxy shrinks the nasal pipes instantly for Emergency Breathing.
cards.lore: Use it for >3 days and you meet Rhinitis-Rebound-Rob—the nose becomes permanently clogged without the drug.
cards.gradeReason: Rhinitis-Rebound-Rob is one of the best named NPCs in the entire corpus. Instantly memorable warning.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: sprinting cheetah character opening nasal passages. Mood: instant relief, three-day warning.

cards.power: THE MOTION-SICKNESS SHIELD. Mick numbs the Balance-Center so the patient can stop vomiting.
cards.lore: Mick doesn't fix the crystals; he just turns down the Brain's Spin-Alarm.
cards.gradeReason: Spin-Alarm is a nice metaphor. H1-blocker mechanism needs the BPPV-Benny context to fully click.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: antihistamine turtle with shield silencing a spinning alarm. Mood: dampening, slow, anti-nausea.

cards.power: THE BYPASS-DRAIN. Mike cuts a hole in Tympanic-Ty and places a tiny pipe to do Eustachian-Earl's job.
cards.lore: Prevents Mitch-Media from returning by keeping the middle ear swamp dry and ventilated.
cards.gradeReason: Bypass-Drain is clear and functional. Works well as the surgical solution card for Mitch.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: tiny tube character drilling bypass hole in eardrum. Mood: precise, mechanical, pediatric.

cards.power: THE EVICTION. Tommy removes the Tonsil-Towers permanently to stop the Strep-Sgt from ever returning.
cards.lore: Post-op risk: The Day-7-Bleed. When the scabs fall off, things can get bloody!
cards.gradeReason: THE EVICTION is perfectly theatrical — day-7 bleeding warning makes this memorable and clinically useful.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: demolition crew evicting two tonsil towers. Mood: explosive, surgical, final.

cards.power: THE CAVE-REBUILD. Frank uses Ned-the-Scope to widen the Ostium-Exits so Sinus-Sid can drain naturally.
cards.lore: Removing the clogs (tissue/polyps) to restore the Aero-Dynamics of the skull.
cards.gradeReason: Cave-Rebuild is a solid role. Functional Endoscopic framing is accurate but less dramatic than other surgeons.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: construction worker character widening sinus drainage exits. Mood: surgical, excavating.

cards.power: THE ULTIMATE-BYPASS. Tray creates a new airway door in the neck, bypassing Emma-Epiglottis and the Mouth-Traffic.
cards.lore: A life-saver for long-term Airway-Assassins or those who can't breathe through the Main-Entrance.
cards.gradeReason: THE ULTIMATE-BYPASS — the drama of a neck airway is immediate. Airway-Assassins is excellent framing.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: emergency door being cut in neck below a blocked airway. Mood: ultimate escape, high stakes.

cards.power: THE SKULL-VIBRATOR. Bob bypasses the Conductive-Bridge entirely by vibrating the skull to talk directly to Cochlea-Cora.
cards.lore: Perfect for patients with no canal or a destroyed Ossicle-Oscar.
cards.gradeReason: THE SKULL-VIBRATOR — immediately strange and memorable. Bone-conduction mechanism is perfectly encoded.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: vibrating bone-anchored device talking directly to skull. Mood: bypassing, resonant, bionic.

cards.power: THE NERVE-PULSE. Clara bypasses Cochlea-Cora entirely, using electrical probes to talk to the brain.
cards.lore: When the Sensor-Failure—Clara doesn't make sound louder; she creates a new Electrical-Language.
cards.gradeReason: Bionic-Ear is compelling but the electrical-language concept needs a moment of explanation.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: bionic cochlear implant character wired directly to auditory nerve. Mood: electrical, futuristic.

cards.power: THE PHANTOM-SCREAM. Tim creates a ringing or buzzing that only the patient can hear.
cards.lore: Often the Cry of dying hair cells in the cochlea. The Brain makes up the sound to fill the silence.
cards.gradeReason: THE PHANTOM-SCREAM is the best power name in the deck. Ghost-Ringer + brain filling silence = G1.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: ghostly cartoon. Subject: ringing ghost bell visible only to one character. Mood: phantom, subjective, lonely.

cards.power: THE WRONG-PIPE-SLIDE. Dot makes food go down the Respiratory-Runway instead of the Esophagus-Road.
cards.lore: Dot is generous to Pneumonia-Pete. Dot is the enemy of the Airway-Sentry.
cards.gradeReason: Wrong-Pipe-Slide is a great image. Aspiration risk needs the Pneumonia-Pete connection to fully land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: food sliding down wrong pipe toward lungs. Mood: wrong way, alarming, aspiration.

cards.power: THE OBJECT-BLOCK. Felix is a bead, a bean, or a coin stuck where it doesn't belong.
cards.lore: In the ear: Do not get the bean wet (it will swell!). In the lung: Unilateral-Wheeze is the clue.
cards.gradeReason: Dual-location (ear vs bronchus) is clinically elegant. Unilateral-wheeze clue is a great pearl.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: bean/coin character lodged in ear vs bronchus dual panel. Mood: stuck, pediatric, urgent.

cards.power: THE SADDLE-NOSE-THREAT. Hank traps blood under the septal skin, cutting off the Cartilage-Food-Supply.
cards.lore: Emergency! If Hank isn't drained, the septum dies, and the nose collapses into a Saddle-Shape.
cards.gradeReason: Saddle-Nose is memorable and specific — trauma context makes this a strong emergency card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: blood pooling under septal skin, cartilage starving. Mood: urgent, post-trauma.

cards.power: THE TONGUE-LIFT. Luke inflames the floor of the mouth until the tongue is pushed up and back, choking the patient.
cards.lore: Usually a Dental-Infection-Riot. Luke is an Airway-Assassin in disguise.
cards.gradeReason: Airway-Assassin in disguise from a dental infection — the betrayal narrative is immediately gripping.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark cartoon. Subject: floor-of-mouth woody swelling lifting tongue upward. Mood: silent threat, choking.

cards.power: THE BONE-ROT. Nick is the Final-Evolution of Ex-Externa. He eats through the ear canal and into the skull.
cards.lore: Nick targets the cranial nerves. If Nick isn't stopped with IV antibiotics, the Brain-Fortress falls.
cards.gradeReason: THE BONE-ROT as Final-Evolution of Ex is brilliant card-game narrative. Diabetic elderly context adds clinical weight.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: dark cartoon. Subject: malignant otitis rotting through skull toward brain. Mood: end-stage, cranial, diabetic.

cards.power: THE ANTIBIOTIC-KEY. The Scribe tells us who gets the Penicillin-Pen and who just needs tea.
cards.lore: Prevents Resistance-Rob by only attacking the Sgt when he's actually present.
cards.gradeReason: Resistance-Rob is a memorable NPC name. Centor criteria framing is clear for clinical reasoning.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: owl scribe scoring a checklist before handing out penicillin. Mood: gatekeeping, decisive.

cards.power: THE BRIDGE-CHECK.
cards.lore: Lateralizes to the bad side? Conduction fail! Lateralizes to the good ear? Sensorineural fail!
cards.gradeReason: Overlaps with Weber & Rinne card 29 — duplicate character with less content. Needs differentiation or cut.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: trio of tuning forks performing bridge inspection. Mood: diagnostic, resonant.

cards.power: THE SOUND-MUFFLE. The patient sounds like they are trying to talk with a scorching hot potato in their throat.
cards.lore: Caused by massive swelling in the oropharynx, preventing normal Sound-Reflection.
cards.gradeReason: Hot-Potato Voice is one of the most embodiable clinical signs in medicine — immediately performable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: patient muffled by giant hot potato in throat, muffled speech bubbles. Mood: garbled, urgent.

cards.power: THE CROUP-CONFIRM. The trachea looks like a church steeple instead of a square pillar.
cards.lore: The trachea looks like a church steeple instead of a square pillar.
cards.gradeReason: Power and lore repeat — this is a sign card that describes rather than invites. Needs distinct LORE revision.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon. Subject: X-ray showing steeple-shaped trachea with croup character. Mood: radiological, narrowing.

cards.power: THE ORIFICE-ORACLE. Doc: Look past the wax. Feel the neck. Is the airway safe? If not, who are you still holding a tongue depressor? Stay fluffy!
cards.lore: MedKayfabe! Stay fluffy!
cards.gradeReason: Doc FrizzleBob as the ENT Attending is a perfect meta-card. The tongue depressor callback is the cherry.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: FrizzleBob cartoon. Subject: rabbit doctor with head mirror and tuning fork. Mood: masterful, fluffy, authoritative.

cards.power: Identify the Media-Mitch and explain why the pain vanished.
cards.lore: A 6-year-old wrestler has a fever and a red, bulging drum. Suddenly, the pain stops and yellow fluid leaks out.
cards.gradeReason: Case-study format is G3 by definition — describes a scenario rather than inviting performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon quiz. Subject: child wrestler with glowing ear, pressure release moment. Mood: diagnostic, quiz.

cards.power: Identify Singer-Sarah and decide: Surgery or Silence?
cards.lore: A lead singer has been hoarse for 2 weeks. The On-the-Scope shows two small bumps at the edges of the white ribbons.
cards.gradeReason: The clinical dilemma format is G3 — but Surgery or Silence? is an excellent framing for the decision.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon quiz. Subject: hoarse singer with vocal scope image. Mood: clinical decision, stage vs clinic.

cards.power: Identify the room spinner and confirm the Epley-Adjustment.
cards.lore: A patient says the room spins for 30 seconds every time they roll out of bed. Weber: to bad ear? Rinne: Bone > Air. Rinne is normal.
cards.gradeReason: Vertigo-Vortex case with audiometry twist is G3 — but the Weber/Rinne integration is a clever trap.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: cartoon quiz. Subject: spinning room with Dix-Hallpike position shown. Mood: vertigo, diagnostic trap.

verdict: ENT: The Sensory Siege is a landmark MedKayfab entry — 56 cards covering the full otolaryngology curriculum from inner-ear anatomy through surgical interventions, with a naming system so consistent you can feel the character in every card name. Named strength: Necrotizing-Nick as the Final-Evolution of Otitis-Externa-Ex is brilliant card-game narrative that would never work in a textbook but burns into memory forever. Named weakness: The Tuning-Fork-Trio (card 50) partially duplicates Weber & Rinne (card 29) and the Steeple-Sign Sentry has identical power and lore text. Three Synthesis Quest cards at the end are G3 by nature but add unique pedagogical value. Table-ready: Yes.
blurb: 56 cartoon characters that make the entire ENT shelf stick — from Tympanic-Ty the Drummer to Necrotizing-Nick the Bone-Rot, with Rhinitis-Rebound-Rob threatening anyone who uses Afrin too long. For med students, residents, and curious humans who want their sinuses explained by a rogue rabbit.

coverQA.coverVisual: 5 — FrizzleBob as ENT attending with tuning fork, colorful exploded-ear anatomy globe, peripheral cartoon creatures. Energetic and immediately communicates ENT.
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — 'ENT: The Sensory Siege' is punchy, alliterative, and series-consistent.
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Carnival-medical chaos tone perfectly matches the deck's villain roster.
coverQA.coverOriginality: 5 — Nothing in medical education looks like this cover. FrizzleBob with a tuning fork is completely distinctive.
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — 'Can you hear the drums, Fernando?' is a great hook but niche. The image travels better than the tagline.
coverQA.coverNote: Best cover in the MedKayfab MegaPack series so far. The tuning fork as FrizzleBob's weapon of choice is perfect ENT symbolism. The 'Stay fluffy!' call-to-action anchors the brand voice cleanly on the very first impression.

notes: 15 pages: 1 cover + 13 standard 2x2 content pages + 1 Wrap Party page (p15) with Doc FrizzleBob + 3 Synthesis Quests. Card 50 (Tuning-Fork-Trio) overlaps significantly with card 29 (Weber & Rinne) — either differentiate by function (29=intro, 50=interpretation algorithm) or cut one. Card 52 (Steeple-Sign Sentry) has identical POWER and LORE text — clear copy-paste error, LORE needs its own content. No RAF boxes. No font artifacts. Landscape format (745x415 pts). Artwork uniformly excellent and consistent. 'KayfaBIZARRO!' / 'KayfaBONGO!' / 'KayfaGOGO!' / 'MedKayfabe!' callout stamps appear on various pages.

urgent: Fix card 52 (Steeple-Sign Sentry): POWER and LORE are identical — LORE needs distinct clinical content, e.g. differential from epiglottitis on X-ray
Differentiate card 50 (Tuning-Fork-Trio) from card 29 (Weber & Rinne) — currently overlapping; consider making card 50 explicitly the interpretation algorithm vs card 29 as the anatomy
quickWins: Label Synthesis Quests as 'Bonus: Case Quest' to set player expectations
Add answer key for Synthesis Quests on a separate page or back-of-card note
niceToHave: Color-code sections: blue anatomy, red pathology, green diagnostics, purple pharmacology, orange surgery
Add cranial nerve walkthrough card (FrizzleBob as CN testing referee)
Rhinitis-Rebound-Rob deserves his own full card

marketingText:
MedKayfab: ENT – The Sensory Siege (Medical Mnemonics Cut & Play Comic)

56 illustrated medical mnemonic cards to master otology, rhinology, and the head-and-neck airway emergencies that decide a patient's hearing, balance, or next breath.

The head and neck is the most expensive real estate in the body. Inside a few cubic centimetres you have got the organ of hearing, the organ of balance, the gatekeeper of the airway, and a cranial-nerve highway, packed so tightly that a lesion the size of a lentil can take a sense away for good. This is the specialty where small things are never small. A blocked nose is an inconvenience until it is the nasal-spray trap that owns you for life. A sore throat is nothing until the flap above the voice box swells and you have seconds, not minutes, to protect the airway.
